newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says two-tier baht market to stay.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says two-tier baht market to stay.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand on Thursday denied market rumours that the authorities would scrap capital controls which led to the creation of a two-tier market for the baht onshore and offshore.
"The rumours are groundless," a senior central bank official told Reuters.
The market rumours suggested that the two-tier baht market would be removed by the end of this week.
The central bank official also declined to say when the two-tier system would be reviewed.

The central bank instituted capital controls in May when the baht came under fierce speculative attack from offshore players. It cut off baht supplies from local sources to foreign speculators forcing then to scramble for the Thai unit to cover short positions built during the attack on the currency.
However, some analysts speculated that the controls could be removed later this year, if and when Thailand gets IMF assistance to put its battered economy back on an even keel.
Thailand is going through its worst economic slump in over a decade. It has so far insisted it will not seek an IMF financial package.
Other analysts said it would be an awkward time now for the authorities to remove the two-tier market because the baht has sunk to new lows and there was a risk it could go lower.
On Thursday the baht plunged to a new low of 32.63 to the dolllar in the domestic market amid strong demand for dollars from commercials and negative sentiment in the market.
The central bank on Wednesday intervened in the market to stem the baht's slide and dealers expected it to do the same on Thursday.
The baht was allowed into a managed float on July 2 by the authorities after being pegged to a trade-weighted basket of currencies dominated by the dollar.
Since the flotation, the baht has undergone a de facto devaluation of about 20 percent.
